title: Personal Credit Cards: Money Still Owed When a Card Closes
content:
What a Personal Credit Cards account still owes at closure decides whether any automatic payment carries on after the card is closed.

## Rule

The automatic payment option left on a closed card is decided from what the card owes at the moment of handling, as the card's current amount owed shows. Where the card owes nothing, or is in credit, the option left is none, because automatic payment runs only until the debt is cleared.

A card that closes while still owing keeps an automatic payment able to collect what remains whenever the cardholder has an active PCB checking account to carry one. Where the cardholder has no such account, the closure goes ahead all the same, and what is owed stays payable on the existing terms, minimum payments included.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical figures)

| Current amount owed | Money still owed | Option left on the closed card |
|---|---|---|
| 0.00 USD | no | none |
| minus 15.00 USD, a credit | no | none |
| 0.01 USD | yes | set by the paying account and the instruction in force |
| 1390.12 USD | yes | set by the paying account and the instruction in force |
